methods.fixtures: tools/spike_m2_fixtures.ts, seed 20261108: synthetic harmonic tone, 5.5 Hz vibrato, note changes, unvoiced gaps with noise; stereo right channel differs (harmonic weights, gain, noise, 0.4 ms delay). Encoder per file in runs[].encoder.
methods.fileInput: Playwright setInputFiles on <input type=file>, then File.arrayBuffer() in the page.
methods.decode: decodeAudioData on an OfflineAudioContext(1, 1, 48000). decodeMs = decodeAudioData call only; readMs = File.arrayBuffer(). The ArrayBuffer and AudioBuffer references are dropped after the channels are posted.
methods.transfer: AudioBuffer.getChannelData arrays posted to a module Worker as transferables (copy fallback reported in result.transferMode).
methods.mix: Worker onmessage: arithmetic mean of all channels per sample into a Float64Array (as tools/wav.ts), timed as worker.mixMs. Analysis is queued with setTimeout(analyse, 0, mono, ...), so the event and its channel arrays are unreachable before analysis starts.
methods.analysis: Worker: new FrameAnalyzer({ sampleRate }).run(mono, true) then decodeAll(frames, { lag: Infinity }), the cont path of tools/run_ts.ts. analysisMs = run + decodeAll (same span run_ts.ts times). realTimeFactor = audio seconds / analysis seconds.
methods.spectrumColumns: Worker, after analysis and timed separately (spectrumColumnsMs): FrameAnalyzer.run does not keep per-frame spectra, so a second pass calls Spectrum.compute (src/dsp/spectrum.ts unchanged, via FrameAnalyzer.spec) at each frame start and copies bins 0..floor(4000 * N / sampleRate) into one Float32Array per frame (171 bins at 48 kHz with N 2048; runs[].result.worker.binsPerColumn).
methods.realisticHold: Worker posts { frames, f0, columns } to the page by structured clone (postCloneMs = the synchronous postMessage call). frames = one object per frame with t, start, voiced, aperiodicity, rmsDb, eSf, eRef (specs/M2.md 4.2 item 6, no YIN candidate arrays); f0 = decoded whole-take f0 as a Float64Array; columns = the spectrum columns. The worker drops its references after posting; the page holds the clone until the tail of sampling ends, then releases it.
methods.memory: Renderer phys_footprint: vmmap -summary "Physical footprint (peak)" read once after the tail (kernel lifetime peak of the process; it includes page load), and footprint -j sampled about every 200 ms for the baseline and timeline. RSS from ps about every 50 ms for the renderer and the whole tree (descendants of the launchServer PID). Baseline = mean over 4000 ms with the page loaded and the Worker started, after a 2500 ms settle, before the file is set; a file whose baseline window has fewer than 10 ps or 5 footprint samples fails and is retried once with a fresh Chrome. Peak window: run plus 1000 ms tail while the page holds the result.
memoryCaveats: phys_footprint counts the renderer only; GPU, browser and utility processes are in the RSS tree column, not in the verdict.
The vmmap lifetime peak has no sampling gaps, but vmmap output is rounded to 0.1 MB and the number includes everything since the renderer started.
RSS leaves out compressed and swapped pages and double-counts shared pages in the tree sum.
Garbage collection timing changes the peak: freed buffers may stay resident until the next GC.
Headless Chrome; a headed tab adds compositor and GPU memory not measured here.
One run per file. Earlier runs, archived in results/_archive/m2_spike_v1/, varied from run to run, and the machine was shared with another session.
methods.timeouts: Per file: 5 x (durationS / 10 + 10 s). A timeout, renderer crash, worker error or page error marks the file failed; that Chrome is closed and the run continues.
